questions.prompt:
Grace drives about 10,000 miles per year and plans to keep a car 5 years. Gas costs $3.75 per gallon. Compare total cost of ownership.
 | Used sedan | New hybrid
Price (tax/fees incl.) | $13,500 | $28,500
Down payment | $2,000 | $2,000
Loan | 7.9% APR, 60 mo | 4.9% APR, 60 mo
Insurance per year | $1,250 | $1,700
Maintenance per year | $1,000 | $350
Fuel economy | 30 mpg | 50 mpg
Resale after 5 yrs | 45% of price | 50% of price
solutionSteps: TCO = down + total of payments + 5 × (insurance + maintenance) + fuel − resale.
Used sedan: $27,382.72.
New hybrid: $31,682.51.
Rubric (16 pts):
Financial accuracy (4): All calculations correct, labeled, and rounded to cents where money is reported.
Use of evidence (4): Cites specific numbers from the scenario or document to support each claim.
Reasoning & tradeoffs (4): Weighs at least two advantages/disadvantages, including a non-numeric factor, and states assumptions.
Recommendation & communication (4): Clear, defensible recommendation; explains what new information would change it. Alternative defensible conclusions earn full credit.

Model response: Over five years the Used sedan costs less ($27,382.72 vs $31,682.51). The hybrid’s fuel savings and lower APR offset part of its higher price, and it keeps more resale value; the used sedan risks larger repairs. Gas prices and resale values are the most uncertain assumptions, so I would rerun the numbers with higher and lower gas prices before deciding.

parts.answer: Answers vary; resale value, repair costs, and gas prices are uncertain.
